_note: Lunar reference per base type. The 0-1 values in scores.csv ARE the similarity to the Moon (1 = equal to the Moon); there are no 0-1 target values. Moon values are raw, in earth_unit. score_method: target = similarity, counts in SCORE_TOTAL if weight > 0; display = similarity shown but weight 0; rank = no lunar value yet, rank within one run, NOT in scores.csv; not computed = no pipeline value yet.

polar.label: Polar base · Shackleton rim + floor (lunar south pole)
polar.total_rule: score (vs Moon): weighted mean of the axes with in_total = true

criteria.label: 1 Sunny ridge
criteria.limitation: Known limitation: on the Moon 'lit' is the visible fraction of the solar DISC (PGDA AVGVISIB, extended Sun); on Earth it is the Sun's CENTRE above the horizon (point Sun). Both give 0.5 on flat land at the pole; on terrain they can differ where the Sun stays partly hidden for long stretches (disc fraction > 0 while the centre is already below the horizon).

moon.source: PGDA product 69 AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608.TIF (Mazarico et al. 2011, LOLA-modelled, 60 m, hourly over 18.6 yr; visible solar-disc fraction)
moon.zone: floor = bowl pixels < 10 deg connected to the low point; rim = outside the bowl, at most 1 km from its edge (criterion-10 zone)
